Successful implementation requires strategic integration and clinical validation: Adoption depends on robust data management, algorithm validation, staff training, workflow integration, and continuous performance monitoring to maintain accuracy and safety. Machine learning is reshaping dentistry by adding intelligent analytical capabilities to daily clinical practice. Instead of relying only on manual interpretation, you can use data-driven insights that identify patterns, predict outcomes, and support evidence-based treatment decisions. These technologies process complex datasets such as radiographs, patient records, and treatment histories to deliver greater precision and efficiency in diagnosis and care planning. By understanding how machine learning applies to dentistry, you can use it to enhance diagnostic accuracy, streamline workflows, and create more personalized treatment plans. Recent research shows that AI-based radiographic analysis can achieve high diagnostic accuracy, often outperforming conventional methods in detecting caries and periapical lesions from radiographs, with sensitivity and specificity rates frequently exceeding 90% in controlled studies. When integrated thoughtfully, machine learning helps you make better-informed clinical decisions while preserving the human connection that defines high-quality dental care. Understanding machine learning applications in dental practice Machine learning is a type of artificial intelligence that learns from data patterns and becomes more accurate over time. In dental practice, it can analyze radiographs, 3D scans, electronic health records, and clinical notes to reveal correlations that might not be visible to the naked eye. You can think of it as a system that helps you interpret information more quickly and consistently. For example, when analyzing radiographs, algorithms trained on thousands of annotated images can accurately identify early lesions, bone loss, or endodontic issues. Machine learning also integrates multiple data types to create a complete picture of a patient’s oral health. By linking radiographs, periodontal measurements, and prior treatment outcomes, it allows you to make decisions based on patterns that extend beyond individual symptoms. This approach supports personalized dentistry grounded in predictive, evidence-based insights. Machine learning applications in dental diagnosis One of the most impactful uses of machine learning in dentistry is improving diagnostic accuracy. These systems apply advanced image recognition and pattern analysis to help you identify conditions more consistently and efficiently. Advanced radiographic image analysis Machine learning algorithms analyze X-rays, cone beam CT scans, and intraoral images to detect early or subtle signs of disease. By recognizing patterns that are difficult for the human eye to distinguish, AI delivers consistent, precise insights that support accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Automated pathology detection and classification AI models can flag abnormalities such as cysts, tumors, or bone changes and classify them for clinical review. This capability supports earlier intervention, clearer diagnosis, and more timely specialist referrals when necessary. By consistently identifying subtle variations across large image datasets, AI helps you reduce oversight and strengthen diagnostic precision in everyday clinical practice. Predictive risk assessment and disease modeling Machine learning can assess the probability of disease progression by analyzing patient data, behavioral factors, and historical outcomes. For example, predictive models can forecast the risk of implant failure or periodontal deterioration, helping you intervene before issues escalate. Clinical decision support and diagnostic assistance Real-time diagnostic tools, such as Pearl’s Second Opinion, use FDA-cleared AI models to analyze radiographs during patient exams. The system highlights potential findings and provides a second layer of confirmation, supporting confident, evidence-based recommendations while maintaining your role as the clinical decision-maker. Quality assurance and diagnostic consistency Machine learning helps maintain consistent diagnostic standards across clinicians and practices. By analyzing performance data, it can identify patterns of underdiagnosis or variability, which supports quality assurance programs and ongoing professional calibration. Continuous algorithm learning and improvement These systems improve over time as they are exposed to new data. Each case contributes to more refined pattern recognition and better predictive power. The result is a continuously learning diagnostic tool that adapts to new evidence, technologies, and patient populations. Treatment planning optimization with machine learning Machine learning can help you create more effective, personalized treatment plans by analyzing patient data, treatment histories, and clinical outcomes. These systems evaluate large amounts of information to predict results, identify risks, and support evidence-based decision-making that leads to higher success rates and greater patient satisfaction. Outcome prediction and success modeling AI-powered tools can analyze thousands of clinical cases to predict the performance of various treatment options. For example, a 2025 Diagnostics review found that machine learning models achieved over 90% predictive accuracy when evaluating orthodontic treatment outcomes using CBCT and patient history data. This allows you to compare possible approaches and discuss likely outcomes with patients more transparently. By integrating predictive models into treatment planning, you can more accurately assess factors such as bone quality, periodontal condition, and patient compliance that impact long-term success. The result is a more tailored plan built on both data and your clinical judgment. Cost-benefit analysis and financial planning Machine learning systems can analyze treatment costs, patient insurance coverage, and predicted success rates to help you plan care that aligns with both patient budgets and practice resources. These insights can support transparent discussions with patients about affordability and expected outcomes, reducing treatment delays caused by financial uncertainty. Interdisciplinary care coordination Complex dental cases often involve collaboration between multiple specialists. Machine learning helps coordinate these efforts by analyzing imaging, treatment sequencing, and interdisciplinary data to optimize timing and outcomes. A 2025 Nature Scientific Reports study demonstrated how reinforcement learning can guide sequential decision-making in orthognathic and orthodontic cases, improving treatment efficiency and predictability. By applying this kind of intelligent coordination, you can streamline communication, avoid redundant procedures, and provide a unified care experience across disciplines. Let's Talk About Your Practice Schedule a Demo Clinical workflow enhancement and automation Beyond diagnosis and treatment planning, machine learning is also transforming the way dental practices operate. By automating repetitive tasks and optimizing workflows, these systems can improve efficiency and reduce administrative strain without sacrificing clinical quality. Automated clinical documentation and record keeping AI-powered platforms can automatically generate treatment notes, summarize radiographic findings, and populate patient records based on structured inputs. This helps reduce manual data entry and ensures more consistent, compliant documentation. Patient communication and engagement optimization Machine learning tools can personalize patient interactions by predicting when reminders, educational content, or follow-up messages are most effective. For example, predictive models can identify which patients are most likely to miss hygiene appointments or delay treatments, helping you intervene before issues arise. Resource optimization and scheduling efficiency Machine learning can help your practice predict chair time, procedure durations, and the likelihood of no-shows based on historical patterns. This makes it easier to schedule patients efficiently, manage staff time, and improve overall productivity. Inventory management and supply chain optimization By tracking consumption trends and upcoming treatment schedules, AI systems can forecast when specific supplies are needed and recommend reorder points. This helps you maintain adequate inventory levels without overstocking. Performance analytics and practice optimization Machine learning can also analyze your practice’s performance metrics to uncover growth opportunities. For instance, algorithms can highlight which procedures generate the most patient satisfaction or identify bottlenecks that slow down case progression. These insights make it easier to refine operations and improve profitability over time. Implementation challenges and considerations While the benefits are clear, integrating machine learning into a dental practice requires careful planning and implementation. You need the right infrastructure, validated tools, and trained staff to use these technologies effectively and ethically. Common challenges include: Data quality and consistency: Systematic reviews of dental AI research note that variation in image quality and anatomical differences across datasets can affect model performance, highlighting the importance of robust training data, consistent preprocessing, and careful clinical validation.

Blog / Article 13 tips to reduce dental insurance denials Pearl Team 6 minute read • January 19, 2026 Insurance Practice Management Key Takeaways Insurance denials can cost dental practices 5%–10% of their annual revenue, resulting in increased administrative work, delayed payments, and frustration for both patients and staff.



Thirteen prevention methods, including eligibility checks, pre-authorizations, accurate coding, thorough documentation, and staff training, form a strong framework for reducing denials.



Front-end prevention is far more effective than back-end appeals. Strong verification and documentation can cut denials by 50%–70%.



Technology tools, such as real-time eligibility verification, claim scrubbing, integrated practice management software, and AI-supported analytics, help identify issues before claims are submitted. Insurance denials create financial and operational strain for dental practices. Each rejected claim forces your team to rework documentation, contact patients, and follow up with payers. These delays slow cash flow and add preventable administrative burden. Over time, unresolved denials turn into real revenue loss. Reducing denials requires strengthening every step of your billing workflow, from patient registration all the way through claim submission. When you combine accurate eligibility checks, strong clinical documentation, proper coding, and supportive technology, you increase clean-claim rates, accelerate payments, and protect the financial stability of your practice. Common causes of dental insurance denials Most denials occur for predictable reasons. Inactive coverage, missing pre-authorizations, outdated CDT codes, incomplete documentation, coordination of benefits errors, and late submissions are among the most common causes. Benefit limitations, such as frequency rules or annual maximums, also contribute to many rejected claims. Because each payer has different rules, tracking denial patterns by insurer and procedure type helps you identify where your workflow needs improvement or where your team needs additional training. The 13 practical ways to reduce dental insurance denials These strategies represent the most effective steps for reducing denials across your revenue cycle. When applied consistently, they significantly increase your first-pass acceptance rate. Verify insurance eligibility before every appointment Use real-time eligibility tools or carrier portals to confirm active coverage, benefit levels, deductible status, and any recent plan changes. Doing this before the appointment reduces the risk of treating patients who are no longer covered or whose plans have changed without their knowledge. Obtain pre-authorization for major procedures High-cost or medically sensitive treatments often require pre-authorization or predetermination. Submitting these requests with correct documentation ensures the payer reviews the clinical need in advance, which lowers the risk of medical-necessity denials later. Maintain accurate and complete patient information Many denials stem from simple registration errors. Confirm that demographic details, subscriber information, policy numbers, and relationships are correct at every visit. Even small discrepancies can cause automatic claim rejections. Document medical necessity thoroughly Strong documentation is the foundation of a defensible claim. Include diagnostic findings, radiographs, periodontal charting, clinical notes, and any supporting evidence that shows why a treatment was necessary. Thorough documentation is especially important for periodontal therapy, extractions, endodontics, and major restorative work. Use correct and specific CDT codes Stay current with CDT updates and choose the code that most accurately describes the procedure performed. Specific coding supports appropriate reimbursement and reduces the chance of automatic denials due to outdated or mismatched codes. Submit complete narrative reports when required For unusual cases or procedures that are not fully explained by codes alone, include a brief narrative that clarifies complexity, clinical reasoning, or special circumstances. This extra context can prevent carriers from requesting additional information later. Include all required attachments and documentation Attach radiographs, photos, periodontal charting, and any required forms at the time of submission. Missing attachments are one of the most common and preventable sources of delay. Verify and manage coordination of benefits (COB) Confirm which plan is primary and which is secondary, then bill in the correct order. Incorrect COB handling often results in automatic denials and requires extra administrative work. Monitor and meet timely filing deadlines Each payer has strict filing limits. Use tracking tools or automated reminders to ensure claims are submitted well before deadlines. Missing these windows usually results in permanent non-payment. Understand and verify fee schedules and benefit limitations Familiarize yourself with the fee schedule for each contracted plan and review the benefit maximums, waiting periods, and frequency rules before treatment. Reviewing these details helps you set realistic expectations with patients and avoid claims that exceed plan limits. Implement systematic claim scrubbing before submission Claim-scrubbing software checks for missing data, coding inconsistencies, expired attachments, and eligibility conflicts. Using these tools before you submit claims significantly increases your clean-claim rate. Train staff continuously on insurance procedures Regular training ensures your team understands coding updates, common denial reasons, payer-specific requirements, and documentation standards. Well-trained staff are your strongest line of defense against preventable denials. Track, analyze, and learn from denials Review denial reports regularly to identify recurring issues. Track denials by payer, reason code, and procedure so your team can make targeted improvements and strengthen weak points in the workflow. Front-end prevention: verification and pre-treatment processes Front-end workflows have the biggest impact on reducing denials. When you verify coverage, check benefits, obtain authorizations, and communicate clearly with patients before treatment, you prevent most issues that would lead to rejections later. Real-time eligibility verification systems Automated eligibility tools provide instant confirmation of active coverage, plan type, remaining maximums, exclusions, and waiting periods. This helps you have conversations with patients who have inactive or restricted benefits before treatment takes place. Pre-treatment benefit verification and estimates Check benefits for upcoming procedures and confirm coverage for specific CDT codes. Then provide a written estimate outlining the expected patient portion and any plan limitations. Pre-authorization and predetermination workflows Identify procedures that require carrier approval. Submit documentation early, track responses, and store approvals in the patient record so they are ready during claim submission. Patient communication about coverage limitations Explain coverage rules, frequency limits, non-covered services, and potential downgrades before treatment begins. Use written consent to document patient understanding and reduce financial misunderstandings. Documentation best practices to support medical necessity Clear, consistent documentation is one of the strongest tools you have for preventing denials. When your clinical notes, images, and records clearly support why a treatment was necessary, payers have less room to question the claim. Comprehensive examination documentation Start with detailed exam findings. Record diagnostic tests, radiographic interpretations, periodontal charting, mobility, existing restorations, and any abnormalities you observe. Strong baseline documentation helps support future claims and justify recommended treatment. Treatment planning documentation Each treatment plan should include the diagnosis, proposed procedures, alternative options, risks discussed, and patient consent. This shows the medical reasoning behind your decisions and supports the necessity of the chosen treatment. Progress notes and treatment records Your notes should clearly reflect what you did at each appointment, including tooth numbers, surfaces, materials used, anesthesia, complications, and post-op instructions. Accurate progress notes help align the services billed with the services actually performed. Photographic and radiographic evidence Attach intraoral photos and the appropriate radiographs for any procedures that are likely to be reviewed. Images help verify clinical findings such as fractures, decay, bone loss, drifting, or failing restorations, making medical necessity easier to prove. How technology helps prevent insurance denials Technology can automate many of the checks that once depended on manual review. When your systems are properly integrated, you reduce errors and create more consistent, predictable claim workflows. Practice management software can embed eligibility checks, flag missing documentation, monitor filing deadlines, and produce denial reports. Claim scrubbing tools review submissions for missing fields, incorrect codes, or required attachments before the claim reaches the payer. Analytics platforms help you identify the most common reasons for denials, high-risk procedures, and payer trends. When you use this data to refine workflows and train your team, your clean-claim rate improves steadily over time. What to do when insurance claims are denied Even with strong prevention systems, denials occasionally happen. What matters is having a clear process for follow-up and appeals. Review the EOB to pinpoint the denial reason, then verify that the submitted information matches your records. Correct any errors or missing fields. If documentation is requested, supply it with a clear explanation of the clinical reasoning. For medical necessity denials you believe are incorrect, prepare a concise appeal that includes your diagnostic findings, supporting images, treatment notes, and references to plan language if appropriate. Track each appeal deadline carefully and document all communication with the payer. For valid denials tied to plan limitations, update your front-end processes to prevent the same issue from recurring with future patients. Building effective staff training and education programs Your denial-prevention system will only be as strong as your team’s understanding of it. Ongoing training ensures consistency across your front desk, clinical, and billing teams. Create a structured training plan that covers coding changes, payer updates, documentation requirements, COB rules, and common reasons for denials. Use real examples from your practice to demonstrate how errors occur and how to prevent them. Cross-train team members so that knowledge is not isolated to a single person. Review denial reports together each month and celebrate improvements. When staff members see how their work impacts revenue and patient satisfaction, they are more invested in keeping claims clean. How Pearl’s Precheck helps reduce insurance denials Precheck is Pearl’s AI-driven eligibility and benefits verification tool that surfaces accurate coverage details before treatment begins. It consolidates information such as active coverage, waiting periods, frequency limits, annual maximums, and code-level benefits so your team can confirm what is covered and where authorization may be required. By catching eligibility issues and benefit restrictions early, Precheck supports cleaner estimates, more complete documentation, and fewer denials caused by missing information or unmet plan requirements. It gives your front office a clearer, more consistent workflow and helps reduce preventable rework in your billing process. Final thoughts Reducing insurance denials is not just about fixing rejected claims. It is about building a stronger, more reliable workflow that catches issues early and prevents them from reaching the payer. When you consistently apply these 13 strategies, you improve clean-claim rates, speed up payments, reduce write-offs, and lower administrative stress. Over time, effective denial prevention becomes a major driver of financial health. You safeguard revenue you have already earned, strengthen patient trust, and create a smoother experience for your entire team. With the right systems and training in place, your practice can operate more efficiently and with far fewer reimbursement surprises. How long do I have to appeal a denied dental insurance claim? Appeal windows vary by payer, but most typically range from 30 to 180 days from the date of denial. Always check the EOB for exact timelines. What are the most common reasons for dental insurance denials? Frequent causes include incorrect or inactive coverage, missing documentation, lack of pre-authorization, coding errors, COB issues, timely filing violations, and plan limitations. Can I bill the patient if insurance denies the claim? Often, yes, depending on the reason for denial and your financial agreement with the patient. Follow payer contracts and ensure that patients have signed a consent form acknowledging their financial responsibility. How can technology help reduce dental insurance denials? 📌 TL;DR: This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about Beyond the Chair: How AI and Machine Learning Are Revolutionizing Dental Diagnostics in 2024, with practical insights for dental practices looking to modernize their patient intake process.





Beyond the Chair: How AI and Machine Learning Are Revolutionizing Dental Diagnostics in 2024

The dental industry is experiencing a technological renaissance, with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) leading the charge in transforming how we diagnose, treat, and manage oral health conditions. As we progress through 2024, these technologies have moved beyond experimental phases into practical, everyday applications that are fundamentally changing the landscape of dental practice.

From automated radiographic analysis to predictive treatment planning, AI-powered diagnostic tools are enhancing accuracy, reducing human error, and enabling earlier detection of dental pathologies. This technological evolution isn't just about replacing human expertise—it's about augmenting clinical decision-making with data-driven insights that improve patient outcomes while streamlining practice operations.

For dental professionals, understanding and implementing these AI-driven diagnostic solutions has become essential for maintaining competitive advantage and delivering optimal patient care. The integration of intelligent systems extends from the initial patient intake process through complex diagnostic procedures, creating a seamless workflow that benefits both practitioners and patients.

AI-Powered Radiographic Analysis: Seeing What the Human Eye Might Miss

Radiographic interpretation has traditionally relied heavily on clinical experience and subjective assessment. Today's AI systems are transforming this process by providing objective, consistent analysis that can detect subtle pathologies often missed during routine examinations. Machine learning algorithms trained on millions of radiographic images can now identify early-stage caries, periodontal bone loss, and even oral cancers with remarkable accuracy.

Leading AI diagnostic platforms like Diagnocat, Pearl AI, and Overjet are demonstrating detection rates that often exceed human performance in controlled studies. For instance, Pearl AI's Second Opinion platform has shown the ability to detect pathology in radiographs with over 90% accuracy, while simultaneously reducing false positives that can lead to unnecessary treatments. These systems analyze bitewing, periapical, and panoramic radiographs in real-time, providing immediate feedback during patient consultations.

Practical Implementation in Daily Practice

The integration of AI radiographic analysis doesn't require a complete overhaul of existing workflows. Most systems integrate seamlessly with existing practice management software and digital imaging systems. When a radiograph is captured, the AI system automatically analyzes the image and flags potential areas of concern with color-coded overlays and confidence scores. This allows dentists to prioritize their attention on areas most likely to require intervention.

Dr. Sarah Chen, a general dentist in Portland, Oregon, reports that implementing AI radiographic analysis has improved her diagnostic confidence, particularly in detecting interproximal caries in posterior teeth. “The system catches things I might have missed, especially in challenging cases with overlapping contacts or dense restorations,” she notes. “It's like having a second pair of expert eyes reviewing every image.”

Predictive Analytics and Risk Assessment: Anticipating Problems Before They Occur

Machine learning algorithms excel at pattern recognition and predictive modeling, making them invaluable for assessing patient risk factors and predicting future oral health outcomes. By analyzing comprehensive patient data—including medical history, lifestyle factors, previous treatment outcomes, and genetic markers—AI systems can identify patients at high risk for specific conditions before clinical symptoms appear.

These predictive models are particularly valuable for periodontal disease progression, caries risk assessment, and treatment outcome prediction. For example, AI systems can analyze factors such as salivary pH, bacterial composition, dietary habits, and oral hygiene compliance to generate personalized risk profiles. This information enables practitioners to implement targeted preventive strategies and customize treatment plans based on individual patient needs.

Integration with Digital Intake Systems

The effectiveness of predictive analytics depends heavily on comprehensive, accurate patient data collection. Modern digital intake systems play a crucial role in this process by systematically gathering relevant health information, lifestyle factors, and patient-reported outcomes. AI-powered intake platforms can automatically identify risk factors and generate preliminary assessments before the patient even enters the operatory.

Advanced intake systems can analyze patient responses to identify inconsistencies, prompt for additional relevant information, and automatically calculate risk scores based on established clinical protocols. This streamlined approach ensures that no critical information is overlooked while reducing the administrative burden on clinical staff.

Treatment Planning and Case Presentation: Data-Driven Decision Making

Photo by Mufid Majnun on Unsplash



AI is revolutionizing treatment planning by analyzing multiple variables simultaneously to recommend optimal treatment sequences and predict outcomes. These systems consider factors such as patient age, medical history, bone density, tooth mobility, and financial constraints to generate comprehensive treatment plans that maximize success probability while minimizing patient burden.

In orthodontics, companies like Align Technology have pioneered AI-driven treatment planning with their ClinCheck software, which uses machine learning to predict tooth movement and optimize aligner design. Similarly, implant planning software now incorporates AI to analyze bone quality, determine optimal implant placement, and predict long-term success rates based on anatomical factors and patient characteristics.

Enhanced Patient Communication

AI-powered treatment planning tools also excel at patient education and case presentation. By generating visual simulations and outcome predictions, these systems help patients understand their conditions and treatment options more clearly. Interactive 3D models, before-and-after simulations, and risk-benefit analyses make complex dental procedures more accessible to patients, leading to improved treatment acceptance rates.

Dr. Michael Rodriguez, an oral surgeon in Denver, has found that AI-enhanced case presentations significantly improve patient understanding and consent rates. “When patients can see a 3D simulation of their implant placement or view predicted healing outcomes, they feel more confident about moving forward with treatment,” he explains. “The visual component, combined with AI-generated success probabilities, makes the decision-making process much clearer.”

Quality Assurance and Continuous Learning: Improving Accuracy Over Time

One of the most compelling aspects of AI diagnostic systems is their ability to continuously learn and improve. Unlike static diagnostic criteria, machine learning algorithms become more accurate as they process more data. This means that AI systems implemented today will become increasingly sophisticated and reliable over time, providing ever-improving diagnostic support.

Quality assurance features built into modern AI systems track diagnostic accuracy, monitor system performance, and provide feedback on clinical outcomes. This creates a continuous improvement loop where the system learns from both successes and failures, refining its algorithms to provide better recommendations for future cases.

Practice Analytics and Performance Monitoring

AI systems also provide valuable practice analytics that help dental professionals understand their diagnostic patterns, treatment outcomes, and areas for improvement. By analyzing aggregate data across multiple cases, these systems can identify trends, highlight successful treatment protocols, and suggest areas where additional training or equipment might be beneficial.

Advanced analytics can track metrics such as diagnostic accuracy rates, treatment success percentages, and patient satisfaction scores, providing objective measures of practice performance. This data-driven approach enables continuous quality improvement and helps practices demonstrate their commitment to evidence-based care to patients and insurance providers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Photo by Atikah Akhtar on Unsplash



How accurate are AI diagnostic systems compared to human dentists?

Current AI diagnostic systems demonstrate accuracy rates that often match or exceed human performance in specific tasks, particularly in radiographic analysis and pattern recognition. However, AI systems are designed to augment rather than replace clinical judgment. The most effective approach combines AI insights with professional expertise, resulting in improved overall diagnostic accuracy compared to either method alone.

What are the costs associated with implementing AI diagnostic tools in a dental practice?

Implementation costs vary significantly depending on the specific AI tools and practice size. Many AI diagnostic platforms operate on subscription models ranging from $200-$800 per month, while others charge per analysis. Most practices report that the improved diagnostic accuracy, increased efficiency, and enhanced patient satisfaction provide a positive return on investment within 6-12 months of implementation.

Do AI diagnostic systems require special training for dental staff?

Most modern AI diagnostic systems are designed with user-friendly interfaces that require minimal training. Basic operation can typically be learned in 1-2 hours, though maximizing the benefits of AI insights may require ongoing education about interpreting results and integrating recommendations into clinical workflows. Many vendors provide comprehensive training programs and ongoing support to ensure successful implementation.

How do patients typically respond to AI-assisted diagnostics?

Patient acceptance of AI diagnostic tools is generally very positive, particularly when the technology is presented as an additional layer of quality assurance rather than a replacement for human expertise. Many patients appreciate the objective, data-driven approach and feel more confident in treatment recommendations supported by AI analysis. Clear communication about how AI enhances rather than replaces clinical judgment is key to patient acceptance.

What data privacy considerations should practices be aware of when implementing AI diagnostics?

AI diagnostic systems must comply with HIPAA regulations and other applicable privacy laws. Practices should ensure that AI vendors provide appropriate data encryption, secure transmission protocols, and clear data usage policies. It's important to verify that patient data is not used for purposes beyond the agreed-upon diagnostic services and that patients are informed about how their data will be utilized in AI analysis.

By: Michael Barbella Managing Editor



A dentist reviews a panoramic radiograph with support from Pearl’s Second Opinion AI. Photo: Business Wire.

Pearl has won U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance for artificial intelligence (AI)-powered detection of dental pathologies on panoramic radiographs. The authorization expands Pearl’s clinically validated radiologic AI technology to the most widely captured extraoral imaging modality in dentistry, and is now available to Second Opinion users in the United States and internationally. SCROLL TO CONTINUE Pearl’s Second Opinion real-time chairside pathology detection platform is now cleared to identify and highlight suspected caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars on panoramic radiographs. Panoramic radiographs present a broad anatomical view that can reveal a wide range of dental and maxillofacial conditions—but their complexity and anatomical distortion can make consistent and accurate pathology detection difficult. This latest FDA clearance validates the performance of Pearl’s radiologic AI applied to one of dentistry’s most diagnostically challenging imaging formats, according to the company. “Panoramic x-rays are increasingly popular because they capture the full mouth with lower radiation than a traditional full-mouth X-ray series, but they remain one of the hardest types of dental X-ray to read reliably,” Pearl Founder/CEO Ophir Tanz stated. “AI brings greater clarity and certainty to pano interpretation. Patients benefit as well: Diagnoses are easier to understand when findings are clearly highlighted and labeled. Although panoramic X-ray adoption in the U.S. still trails the U.K. and Europe, this FDA clearance affirms the strength of our technology and moves the industry closer to universal AI support across dental radiology.” The FDA clearance is supported by extensive clinical validation, including a standalone performance study and a fully crossed multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) trial demonstrating that Second Opinion significantly improves detection of caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars. Across all study subgroups—including gender, geography, and imaging device type—the AI maintained stable, unbiased performance. For current Second Opinion users in the United States and internationally, panoramic AI support is available both within Pearl’s standalone software and across dozens of imaging and practice management systems where Second Opinion is natively integrated to support seamless adoption within existing clinical workflows. Pearl is an AI-driven company committed to enhancing patient care in dentistry. Founded in 2019 by a team with decades of experience developing successful, enterprise-grade computer vision solutions, Pearl introduced the first FDA-cleared AI capable of reading and instantly identifying diseases in dental X-rays. With regulatory clearance in 120 countries, Pearl’s AI assists dentists in making precise clinical decisions and effectively communicating with patients, thereby transforming the dental care experience worldwide.

data.title: Pearl Raises Largest-Ever Investment in Dental AI with $58 Million Round
data.ai_summary: Pearl raised $58 million in Series B funding led by Left Lane Capital, the largest investment in dental AI. The company will use the funds to expand its AI product line, regulatory portfolio, and global access. Pearl's AI is FDA-cleared and used in over 500,000 dental practices.
data.full_text:
Megan Cahalan
Matter Health for Pearl
Pearl@matternow.com
The landmark investment in dental artificial intelligence enables Pearl to further expand its dental AI solutions and meaningfully improve oral health outcomes for patients
(BUSINESS WIRE)--Pearl, the global leader in dental AI, today announced that it has raised $58 million in Series B funding to accelerate its mission to elevate patient care in dentistry. Left Lane Capital led the round, with participation from Smash Capital, Alpha Partners, and existing investors, Craft Ventures and Neotribe Ventures. This funding marks the largest investment ever in dental artificial intelligence.
With this investment, Pearl will continue to advance innovation in technologies that enhance the health of dental patients around the world by expanding its line of dental AI products, broadening its regulatory and patent portfolio, and increasing global access to the transformative benefits of AI in dentistry. At present, Pearl’s machine learning and computer vision tools solve a core challenge in dentistry: inconsistency in diagnostic accuracy, which directly impacts the quality of patient care. The company’s AI serves as a real-time aid to help dentists read patient x-rays, deliver consistent, objective, and accurate diagnoses, and clearly communicate findings to patients with precision, clarity, and confidence.
Since receiving the first-ever FDA clearance for AI software to help dental professionals detect multiple different pathologies and other conditions in x-rays, Pearl’s clinical AI has gained regulatory authorizations for chairside use in over 120 countries and recognition among TIME’s Best Inventions. The company plans to use the funding announced today both to accelerate ongoing development of computer vision capabilities – including detection and tracking of disease in 3D and other imaging modalities – and introduce new AI tools to improve patient treatment planning, insurance claim approvals and dental education.
“In the field of healthcare, dentistry has become an AI standard-bearer, demonstrating the technology’s enormous utility and benefit in day-to-day patient care––and Pearl has led the AI charge in dentistry,” said Ophir Tanz, founder and CEO of Pearl. “This historic funding round underscores the impact of Pearl’s capabilities and supports our belief that high-quality, AI-powered dental care should be accessible to everyone. With this investment, Pearl will continue to push the envelope, providing pioneering machine learning to improve oral health outcomes and strengthen trust between the patient and dental professionals.”
This investment follows a period of significant growth for Pearl. The company grew its revenue by 458% in 2023 and remains the only dental AI company with a global market presence. Pearl’s technology is used in dental practices across six continents and is commercially available to over 500,000 dental practices and millions of dental professionals worldwide. The company has also integrated its AI into dozens of popular imaging and practice management systems and is the preferred radiologic AI provider for leading dental technology distributors.
“We have spent the past year evaluating this market and it is clear that Pearl stands above peers at the forefront of dental innovation,” said Vinny Pujji, Managing Partner at Left Lane Capital. “Pearl’s pioneering dental Al improves diagnostic accuracy and efficiency while transforming the provider-patient relationship. We’re confident in Pearl’s ability to continue setting new standards of care and are thrilled to support their next phase of growth.”
Pearl’s AI technology offers a seamless and less invasive approach to dental diagnostics. By accurately detecting disease and displaying clinical findings that are easy for patients to understand, the company’s FDA-cleared software enhances the efficiency, consistency, and precision of radiologic exams, while also facilitating patient education and engagement in their dental health. Leveraging its new funding, Pearl will enable dental professionals to continually raise the standard of care with more transparent, accurate and objective diagnoses, more effective individualized care, and deeper patient trust in dentistry.
For more information on how Pearl’s suite of solutions can enhance your dental practice, visit hellopearl.com.
About Pearl
Pearl is an AI-driven company committed to enhancing patient care in dentistry. Founded in 2019 by a team with decades of experience developing successful, enterprise-grade computer vision solutions, Pearl introduced the first-ever FDA-cleared AI capable of reading and instantly identifying diseases in dental x-rays. With regulatory clearance in 120 countries, Pearl’s AI assists dentists in making precise clinical decisions and effectively communicating with patients, thereby transforming the dental care experience worldwide. As dentistry’s global AI leader, Pearl is committed to the ongoing innovation of robust, accessible AI tools that improve patient health outcomes and build greater trust in dental medicine. To request a demo, please visit hellopearl.com/getdemo.
About Left Lane Capital
Founded in 2019, Left Lane Capital is a New York and London-based global venture capital and growth equity firm investing in internet and technology companies with a consumer orientation. Left Lane’s mission is to partner with extraordinary entrepreneurs who create category-defining companies across growth sectors of the economy, including software, healthcare, e-commerce, consumer, fintech, medtech, and other industries. Select investments include Bilt Rewards, Polycam, Kings League, M1 Finance, Wayflyer, Masterworks, Blank Street, Talkiatry, LemFi, and more. For more information, please visit www.leftlane.com.

data.full_text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing how dental practices understand and use their data. Instead of relying on static reports or intuition, modern AI platforms turn raw operational, clinical, and financial data into meaningful insights that drive better decision-making, patient outcomes, and profitability. With AI-powered analytics, you can uncover hidden trends, optimize daily operations, anticipate patient needs, and make evidence-based choices. This helps you identify growth opportunities, streamline workflows, and build a stronger foundation for long-term success. Understanding AI analytics capabilities for dental practice data AI analytics brings a level of precision and speed that traditional methods can’t match. It allows you to analyze thousands of data points at once, recognizing connections that would take hours or days to uncover manually. These systems use deep learning models trained on dental practice data to identify relationships among patient behavior, financial performance, and operational efficiency. Over time, they learn to predict future trends, recommend improvements, and give you actionable insights to guide both clinical and business decisions. Time-intensive manual data review limitations When data analysis is done manually, it consumes valuable time and resources. Compiling and interpreting appointment histories, production reports, and treatment outcomes can become overwhelming, preventing you from fully leveraging the information your practice already collects. Multi-variable correlation and complex pattern recognition AI can evaluate multiple variables at once, something that’s nearly impossible to do consistently without automation. It identifies connections between patient demographics, treatment acceptance, and practice revenue that human review might overlook. Predictive modeling and future trend forecasting Unlike traditional reporting, which focuses solely on past results, AI predicts future outcomes. It can forecast seasonal appointment trends, patient demand, and potential declines in case acceptance before they impact your bottom line. Real-time insights and dynamic monitoring Manual reporting gives you historical data, not live intelligence. AI analytics works continuously, identifying real-time changes and allowing you to act immediately when trends or anomalies appear. Comprehensive data integration across systems Many dental practices use separate tools for scheduling, imaging, billing, and patient communication. AI brings these systems together, enabling a complete and unified view of your practice performance. Subtle trend identification and early warning indicators AI analytics can detect small, gradual shifts, such as declining hygiene recall rates or slightly longer chair times, that may go unnoticed during routine reviews. Recognizing these early helps you take preventive action. Objective performance benchmarking AI tools allow you to compare performance metrics across providers, time periods, and locations. This gives you objective benchmarks for evaluating productivity and quality and helps set measurable improvement goals. Advanced AI capabilities for practice data intelligence AI analytics does far more than summarize numbers. It turns those numbers into strategy. By combining pattern recognition, predictive modeling, and natural language processing, AI provides multi-dimensional insights that support better business and clinical decisions. When applied effectively, these systems can analyze patient interactions, financial cycles, and workflow data in real time, creating a living picture of your practice’s performance. This allows you to move from reactive management to proactive leadership. Patient behavior analysis and retention prediction AI reviews appointment histories, communication records, and payment behaviors to identify patients who may be at risk of leaving the practice. With that knowledge, you can refine your outreach strategies, enhance engagement, and boost retention rates. Treatment pattern analysis and clinical optimization Machine learning helps you evaluate which procedures and treatment sequences produce the best outcomes. By understanding what works best for your patients, you can standardize protocols that improve efficiency and patient satisfaction. Revenue cycle optimization and financial forecasting AI-powered financial analytics examine billing data, claims, collections, and seasonal trends to identify bottlenecks and forecast revenue performance. With accurate forecasting, you can plan investments and manage cash flow more effectively. Scheduling efficiency and capacity utilization AI systems analyze your scheduling data to identify open chair time, recurring cancellations, and peak booking patterns. You can use these insights to optimize appointment slots and improve daily production. Operational bottleneck identification and workflow optimization By evaluating clinical and administrative workflows, AI detects where time, resources, or communication breaks down. Fixing these bottlenecks can boost team productivity and improve the overall patient experience. Clinical benefits of AI-extracted practice insights AI doesn’t just improve your operations, it also strengthens clinical excellence. By combining performance data with patient outcomes, you gain a clearer view of what works best in your treatment approach and where you can improve. These insights allow you to deliver higher-quality care, enhance patient trust, and continuously refine your practice protocols based on measurable evidence. Treatment success analysis AI identifies patterns that lead to consistently successful outcomes. It helps you understand which treatments, techniques, or materials deliver the best results so that you can replicate success across cases. Patient risk assessment By analyzing health records and treatment histories, AI can predict which patients are at risk of developing certain oral health conditions, enabling early intervention and preventive care. Clinical productivity metrics AI tracks how efficiently procedures are performed, how long appointments take, and how each provider’s productivity compares over time. These insights help you improve clinical performance and team balance. Quality assurance monitoring AI ensures consistent standards of care by detecting deviations from established protocols. This supports internal quality assurance and helps maintain patient confidence in your practice. Best practices for AI analytics system implementation To get full value from AI insights, your practice needs a clear and organized rollout. Start by ensuring your data is clean and consistent, with accurate treatment, scheduling, and billing entries across all systems. Train your team on proper data input and how to spot integrity issues. Integrate your AI platform with your practice management and imaging systems so information flows smoothly. Establish clear protocols for who reviews insights, how findings are interpreted, and when actions are taken. Build regular review sessions into your workflow to discuss AI-generated insights as a team. Maintain strong security and compliance by meeting HIPAA, GDPR, or other local requirements. Document how patient data is used, set appropriate access levels, and monitor for errors or irregularities. Treat implementation as ongoing. Set measurable performance goals, track your results, and refine your processes as your AI system learns and your data matures. Future advancements in AI dental practice analytics What you’re doing now is just the beginning. In the near future, AI analytics in your practice will evolve in scope and sophistication. You’ll see deeper predictive capabilities that tell you not only what has happened and what is happening, but also what is likely to happen next. Expect seamless integration of clinical imaging, wearable health data, patient-reported outcomes, and genomic or systemic-health indicators. This expanded data horizon will allow you to tailor preventive-care strategies, personalize treatment plans, and predict patient behavior with greater accuracy. Real-time analytics will increasingly become standard: dashboards that update live during the patient day, alerts when key metrics shift (such as hygiene recall drop-off or case acceptance decline), and automated recommendations sent to your team. How Pearl enables data-driven insights for your practice Pearl offers a purpose-built platform to help you translate AI analytics into action in your dental practice. With Practice Intelligence, Pearl’s AI takes your existing radiographic, scheduling, and treatment data and produces actionable insights into performance, opportunity, and efficiency. Practice Intelligence integrates with your practice management system and imaging modules to pull in multiple data streams, analyzes them with machine-learning models trained on extensive annotated dental data, and delivers dashboards that show where your practice is performing well and where it is missing opportunities. For example, Pearl’s AI can identify patients who have radiographic indications of untreated conditions (via its core AI detection product, Second Opinion) and cross-check them against existing treatment plans or schedules, thereby highlighting case-acceptance gaps. By adopting Pearl’s analytics tools, you’re positioned to move from intuition-based decisions to data-driven strategy: you can optimize scheduling, increase case acceptance, monitor clinician performance, reduce bottlenecks, and improve both patient outcomes and practice profitability. FAQs How much practice data is needed for AI to generate useful insights? You can start getting useful insights as soon as your AI is connected to your PMS and imaging software. Insight depth improves as more historical data is available. What types of insights can AI extract from dental practice management software? AI can surface unscheduled indicated care, overdue recalls, scheduling gaps, trends in case acceptance and production, and workflow issues that affect efficiency. Can AI insights improve both clinical outcomes and practice profitability? AI helps you make data-informed clinical and operational decisions about standardizing review of radiographs, prioritizing indicated care, tightening eligibility/claims, and optimizing schedules, which can support better care and healthier financial performance. How quickly can practices see results from AI-generated insights? Many practices see early operational wins once they act on surfaced unscheduled care and scheduling gaps. data.full_text: LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Pearl, the global leader in AI solutions for dentistry, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for AI-powered detection of dental pathologies on panoramic radiographs. This latest clearance expands Pearl’s clinically validated radiologic AI technology to the most widely captured extraoral imaging modality in dentistry, and is now available to Second Opinion® users in the U.S. and internationally. This clearance marks another major advancement in the company’s mission to elevate diagnostic accuracy, consistency, and efficiency across the full spectrum of dental care. Pearl’s Second Opinion real-time chairside pathology detection platform is now FDA cleared to identify and highlight suspected caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars on panoramic radiographs. Share Pearl’s Second Opinion real-time chairside pathology detection platform is now cleared to identify and highlight suspected caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars on panoramic radiographs. Panoramic radiographs present a broad anatomical view that can reveal a wide range of dental and maxillofacial conditions—but their complexity and anatomical distortion can make consistent and accurate pathology detection difficult. This latest FDA clearance validates the performance of Pearl’s radiologic AI applied to one of dentistry’s most diagnostically challenging imaging formats. “Panoramic x-rays are increasingly popular because they capture the full mouth with lower radiation than a traditional full-mouth x-ray series, but they remain one of the hardest types of dental x-ray to read reliably,” said Ophir Tanz, founder and CEO of Pearl. “AI brings greater clarity and certainty to pano interpretation. Patients benefit as well: Diagnoses are easier to understand when findings are clearly highlighted and labeled. Although panoramic x-ray adoption in the U.S. still trails the U.K. and Europe, this FDA clearance affirms the strength of our technology and moves the industry closer to universal AI support across dental radiology.” The FDA clearance is supported by extensive clinical validation, including a standalone performance study and a fully crossed multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study demonstrating that Second Opinion significantly improves detection of caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars. Across all study subgroups—including gender, geography, and imaging device type—the AI maintained stable, unbiased performance. With this clearance, Pearl strengthens its position as the most comprehensive FDA-cleared radiologic AI platform in dentistry, spanning bitewing, periapical, panoramic, and CBCT imaging. For current Second Opinion® users in the U.S. and internationally, panoramic AI support is available both within Pearl’s standalone software and across dozens of imaging and practice management systems where Second Opinion is natively integrated to support seamless adoption within existing clinical workflows. About Pearl Pearl is an AI-driven company committed to enhancing patient care in dentistry. Founded in 2019 by a team with decades of experience developing successful, enterprise-grade computer vision solutions, Pearl introduced the first-ever FDA-cleared AI capable of reading and instantly identifying diseases in dental x-rays. With regulatory clearance in 120 countries, Pearl's AI assists dentists in making precise clinical decisions and effectively communicating with patients, thereby transforming the dental care experience worldwide. As dentistry’s global AI leader, Pearl is committed to the ongoing innovation of robust, accessible AI tools that improve patient health outcomes and build greater trust in dental medicine. data.full_text:
Pearl has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for the use of artificial intelligence to assist in the detection of dental pathologies on panoramic radiographs. The clearance extends the company’s previously validated radiologic AI technology to panoramic imaging, the most commonly used extraoral radiographic modality in dentistry. The cleared functionality is available to users of the Second Opinion® platform in the United States and internationally.

With this clearance, Second Opinion is authorized to identify and visually indicate suspected caries, periapical radiolucencies, and impacted third molars on panoramic radiographs. Panoramic imaging provides a comprehensive view of the maxillofacial region, but anatomical overlap and image distortion can make interpretation variable. The FDA’s decision reflects an evaluation of the system’s performance in this diagnostically complex imaging format.

“Panoramic x-rays are increasingly popular because they capture the full mouth with lower radiation than a traditional full-mouth x-ray series, but they remain one of the hardest types of dental x-ray to read reliably,” said Ophir Tanz, founder and CEO of Pearl. “AI brings greater clarity and certainty to pano interpretation. Patients benefit as well: Diagnoses are easier to understand when findings are clearly highlighted and labeled. Although panoramic x-ray adoption in the U.S. still trails the U.K. and Europe, this FDA clearance affirms the strength of our technology and moves the industry closer to universal AI support across dental radiology.”

The clearance is supported by clinical validation data, including a standalone performance study and a fully crossed multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study. These evaluations demonstrated improved detection of the specified conditions when clinicians used the AI system. Performance consistency was observed across analyzed subgroups, including gender, geographic region, and imaging device type.

This authorization adds panoramic radiographs to the range of imaging modalities for which the platform has received FDA clearance, alongside bitewing, periapical, and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. Panoramic AI functionality is accessible through Pearl’s standalone software as well as through integrations with multiple imaging and practice management systems, allowing use within existing clinical workflows.

Finding investors who get dental economics Experience: Look for funds that backed at least two dental companies past Series A. DSO investors often don't understand practice management software gross margins. Software investors miss the insurance reimbursement complexity, both of which matter when scaling operations similar to how nonprofit models handle constrained margins. Network: Ask if they can intro you to regional DSOs or dental insurance payers. Those relationships matter far more than big-name logos, especially if you need warm introductions that avoid messy outreach tactics. Alignment: Dental practices have 6-12 month software adoption cycles. Funds expecting 3-month enterprise sales will push you toward bad pricing or distribution decisions that kill gross margins. Track record: Check if their portfolio companies got acquired by DSOs or scaled independently. Most failed dental tech startups died trying to sell directly to individual dentists instead of going through groups. Be careful of other GDPR pitfalls when handling sensitive practice data. Communication: Use Ellty to share your deck with trackable links. You'll see who actually opens your DSO partnership slides versus just looking at dentist testimonials. Value-add: Generic promises about "connections to healthcare systems" don't help if you're selling intraoral camera software. Ask for specific intros to DSO CTOs or dental insurance medical directors. Reaching dental tech investors efficiently Identify potential investors: Check Crunchbase for funds that led rounds in Overjet, Pearl, or Dental Intelligence. Don't pitch general healthcare funds unless you have clear clinical outcomes data. Most won't understand dental practice workflows or equipment financing models. Craft a compelling pitch: Show practice adoption rates and revenue per location for DSO plays, or dentist retention and usage frequency for software. Investors are tired of patient satisfaction scores without proof that practices will pay or that insurance covers your solution. Share your pitch deck: Upload to Ellty and send trackable links. Monitoring how long investors spend on your reimbursement slides gives you clarity, much like confirming password protection is enabled for sensitive financial documents. Utilize your network: Message founders from Dandy, Overjet, or Dental Intelligence on LinkedIn. Ask which funds helped with DSO introductions versus which just wanted consumer traction metrics that don't matter for B2B dental. Attend networking events: Chicago Dental Society Midwinter Meeting and Dentsply Sirona World are where DSO executives and investors actually meet. Skip generic digital health conferences unless you're purely telehealth. Engage on online platforms: Connect with partners after getting a warm intro from a portfolio founder in dental. Cold messages to dental tech investors rarely work because the space is tight-knit and everyone knows everyone. Organize due diligence: Set up an Ellty data room with your DSO contracts, state licensing documentation, and practice adoption data before they ask. It speeds up the process and shows you understand regulatory complexity. Set up introductory meetings: Lead with your economics per practice location or per dentist, depending on your model. Don't waste 20 minutes explaining the dentist shortage. They already know the market dynamics. Why dental tech matters in 2026 Dental tech funding hit $2.1B in 2025, up from $1.8B in 2024. DSO consolidation drove half of that capital. The shift from individual practice software to DSO-wide platforms is real and accelerating. AI-powered diagnostics, digital lab workflows, and DSO enabling software raised the most capital in early 2026. Direct-to-consumer aligners cooled after SmileDirectClub's struggles, but practice management and imaging platforms are growing. Avoid funds still chasing the Invisalign model unless you have fundamentally different distribution.

Uncategorized Staffing Key Dental Industry Trends: What Practice Owners Need to Know In 2025, dental industry trends such as AI and 3D printing technologies, and the increasing consolidation of practices, are keeping practice owners and managers on their toes. Understanding these trends will help you stay competitive and efficient. And with the dental market projected to grow substantially over the coming years, now is the perfect time to use these trends to modernize your practice and embrace the future of dental care. Jan 15, 2025

1. Digital Transformation and Technology Integration





AI and Machine Learning Revolution Dental practices are seeing a big shift as AI and machine learning become essential tools. Leading companies like Pearl, Diagnocat, and 3Shape Automate are transforming diagnostic capabilities through AI-powered analysis of radiographs and intraoral images. AI-powered diagnostic systems can rapidly detect various conditions with high accuracy, from tooth decay to bone loss. AI goes beyond diagnostics; it helps in treatment planning and automation. For example, AI-driven crown design systems can automatically create precise restoration plans, cutting down the planning time significantly while keeping accuracy high. AI also helps in making better decisions by analyzing vast amounts of clinical data to suggest the best treatment approaches. Advanced 3D Printing Applications 3D printing has gone from a novelty to a must-have in dental practices. New advancements now allow for printing permanent restorations. Companies like SprintRay are pioneering innovations in 3D-printed permanent crowns, offering practices the ability to deliver same-day restorations. The technology enables in-house manufacturing of various dental devices, from surgical guides to clear aligners, reducing laboratory costs and treatment times. New dental resins keep expanding what's possible, improving the strength and look of printed restorations. These advancements help practices offer more affordable solutions without sacrificing quality. Digital Imaging and CAD/CAM Evolution Digital imaging and CAD/CAM technology have reached a tipping point in adoption, with over 50% of practices in the USA now utilizing intraoral scanners . This widespread adoption is changing traditional workflows—many laboratory cases in the United States now begin with digital impressions. These technologies create a smooth digital workflow that links imaging, planning, and making restorations. Modern intraoral scanners provide highly accurate 3D images, eliminating the discomfort of traditional impressions while improving precision. When combined with CAD/CAM systems, these digital impressions enable the rapid production of highly accurate restorations, often in a single visit. Cloud-based platforms connect these various technologies, allowing practices to access patient data, treatment plans, and digital designs from anywhere. Practice Management and Staffing Solutions The dental industry is facing an unprecedented staffing crisis that's reshaping how practices approach workforce management. The staffing shortage has reduced practice capacity nationwide. The scope of this challenge is staggering. By connecting with vetted dental hygienists through our platform, you can keep your practice running smoothly while giving dental staff the flexibility they value. Interstate Mobility The Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact , enacted in several states, is creating new opportunities for workforce mobility. The compact reduces licensing barriers across state lines, helping practices access a broader talent pool and professionals find opportunities in areas with the greatest need. Dental staffing is particularly challenging given that 34% of dental hygienists plan to retire within six years . The impending wave of retirements, combined with declining enrollment in dental programs, makes it crucial for practices to adapt their management strategies now to ensure long-term sustainability. 3. Patient-Centric Care Evolution The dental industry is moving toward more patient-focused care delivery, driven by technological advances and changing patient expectations. Teledentistry: Expanding Access and Convenience Teledentistry supports virtual consultations for minor issues and remote monitoring of post-operative progress. It allows patients to receive initial assessments, follow-up care, and ongoing monitoring without leaving their homes. data.title: Pearl Expands Pediatric Capabilities with Second Opinion® for Kids
data.ai_summary: Pearl, a dental AI company, announced the launch of Second Opinion® for Kids, expanding its AI-powered radiologic detection platform with a kid-friendly interface designed to help dentists identify dental disease in young patients as young as four. The new tool displays AI-detected cavities as "sugar bugs" to make it easier for dentists to communicate findings with children and parents, addressing challenges in pediatric care including young patients' limited ability to express discomfort and difficulty earning their cooperation. data.full_text:
Pearl Expands Pediatric Capabilities with Second Opinion® for Kids

Share

AI-powered early decay detection offers a new standard for children’s dental care at an unprecedented inflection point in pediatric dentistry

Second Opinion® for Kids displays AI-detected cavities as "sugar bugs", making it easier for dentists to explain oral health to young patients.

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Pearl, the global leader in dental AI solutions, today announced Second Opinion® for Kids, expanding the pediatric capabilities of its flagship radiologic AI platform. This launch marks a pivotal advancement in children’s oral healthcare, introducing a new, kid-friendly interface that builds on Pearl’s proven real-time disease detection capabilities. Building on Second Opinion’s existing pediatric functionality – which helps dentists identify disease in patients as young as four, when treatment is simpler, less invasive, and more effective – Second Opinion for Kids further enhances communication between dentists, parents, and children to support more engaging and educational oral health discussions. Second Opinion for Kids further enhances communication between dentists, parents, and children to support more engaging and educational oral health discussions. Share “Second Opinion for Kids reflects our commitment to delivering technology that empowers pediatric dentists to intervene earlier, communicate more clearly, and ultimately give children the best possible start to lifelong oral health,” said Ophir Tanz, CEO of Pearl. “As the son of a dentist, I’ve understood from an early age how critical trust and early intervention are in shaping a child’s experience with dentistry. With Second Opinion for Kids, we’re helping dentists meet the clinical and emotional stakes of pediatric care at a time when proactive, evidence-based solutions are more important than ever.” Pediatric dentistry plays a crucial role in establishing lifelong oral health, yet it presents unique challenges—from young patients’ limited ability to communicate discomfort to the difficulty of earning their trust and cooperation in the chair. Early, accurate diagnosis and clear communication with both children and parents are essential to building those foundations. Second Opinion® for Kids supports that mission by giving dentists a more intuitive, engaging way to visualize and explain findings—helping to reduce anxiety, improve understanding, and foster positive oral health habits from an early age.
